issues.legal_issue: A payment for an exclusive, enduring right to fish for goods in a defined area is capital expenditure when it secures a source for obtaining stock-in-trade rather than the stock itself.
material_facts: The assessee carried on a business of buying and selling conch shells, and also obtained shells by fishing.
It paid rent under a three-year lease granting an exclusive right to fish for and take specified shells from an extensive coastal area.
The lease secured a right to fish, not a specified quantity of shells; the shells might or might not be found and brought to the surface.
The assessee sought to deduct the lease payment as business expenditure, and the appeal concerned the refusal of that deduction.
issues.conclusion: The majority held that the lease payment was capital expenditure and was not deductible from business profits. The appeal was allowed.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 10(2)(xv) of the Income-tax Act, 1922, expenditure laid out wholly and exclusively for business is not deductible if it is capital in nature. The distinction depends on the nature of the business, the expenditure, the right acquired, and their relationship; an enduring asset or source from which stock-in-trade is obtained points to capital expenditure, while expenditure for acquiring the stock itself may be revenue expenditure. The Court applied the approach in Assam Bengal Cement Co. Ltd. v. Commissioner of Income-tax and Pringle Industries Ltd. v. Commissioner of Income-tax, and distinguished Mohanlal Hargovind v. Commissioner of Income-tax because that case concerned acquisition of the raw material itself rather than an enduring right to fish for a source of stock.

rule.if: income_tax_deduction_appeal and dealer_sells_goods and lease_grants_exclusive_fishing_right and lease_covers_extensive_area and right_is_for_a_substantial_period and goods_are_not_secured_in_a_specified_quantity

predicates.income_tax_deduction_appeal: The proceeding is an income-tax appeal concerning whether a business payment may be deducted from profits.
predicates.dealer_sells_goods: The taxpayer conducts a business of selling goods and also obtains goods by fishing or gathering them.
predicates.lease_grants_exclusive_fishing_right: The taxpayer obtains an exclusive right to fish for and take goods from an area.
predicates.lease_covers_extensive_area: The right obtained applies to an extensive area from which the taxpayer may fish or gather goods.
predicates.right_is_for_a_substantial_period: The right obtained continues for a substantial period rather than applying only to a short, immediate collection.
predicates.goods_are_not_secured_in_a_specified_qua: The agreement does not secure a specified quantity of goods, which may or may not be found and collected.

issues.definition: When a goods-selling business in an income-tax deduction appeal pays for an exclusive, substantial-period right to fish over an extensive area without securing a specified quantity of goods, the payment is treated as capital expenditure and is not deductible.
